manifest.name: gdn-fp8-mid24-35-lmhead-q4k
manifest.description: The shipped NVFP4 map with two changes: FP8 on the recurrent projections of layers 24-35 only, and lm_head stored BF16 so its batch-1 Q4_K is fitted once from the original weights. Every recipe that lowers drift so far gives up a sixth to a half of prompt reading, because Q4_K on the recurrent path or the MLP, or FP8 on the whole recurrent path, moves prefill off the shipped NVFP4 kernels. Measured on a pinned RTX 5090, FP8 on this one mid-depth band (27 projections, 4% of the searchable weights) is where the 8 bits pay: it lowers drift in every section, most in long context, while prefill stays within about 3% of V0 and decode within about 2.5%. Wider bands (20-39, 24-47, 16-47) lower drift a little more but cost decode and prefill in proportion to the FP8 bytes; a narrower one (24-31) gives up most of the gain. Every other recurrent layer, attention and the MLP keep the shipped bytes.
